questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Muscarinic antagonist that dries secretions and reverses bronchorrhoea and bradycardia; titrated until the chest is clear.

options.label: B
options.explanation: An anticholinesterase that would add to acetylcholine excess; it is used for anticholinergic (atropine) poisoning, not OPC.

options.label: C
options.explanation: An oxime that reactivates phosphorylated acetylcholinesterase if given before 'ageing' of the enzyme.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Airway clearance and high-flow oxygen are part of initial resuscitation, as respiratory failure is the usual cause of death.

questions.pearl: OPC: atropinise to a dry chest, HR >80 and SBP >80; give pralidoxime early, benzodiazepines for seizures.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Drug safe for diabetes mellitus in pregnancy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sulfonylureas cross the placenta and risk neonatal hypoglycaemia; not the standard choice in pregnancy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: No adequate pregnancy safety data and risk of fetal hypoglycaemia; avoided.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Crosses the placenta; used as an adjunct in some guidelines, but insulin remains the drug of choice in classic teaching.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Large peptide that does not cross the placenta; the gold-standard therapy for diabetes in pregnancy.

questions.pearl: Insulin is the drug of choice for diabetes in pregnancy because it does not cross the placenta.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Central alpha-2 agonist with the longest safety record in pregnancy; a first-line oral agent.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nifedipine is a recommended first-line agent for both chronic and acute severe hypertension in pregnancy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Reduce plasma volume, which is already contracted in pre-eclampsia, and may impair placental perfusion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Associated with fetal growth restriction when used early and long term; labetalol is preferred among beta-blockers.

questions.pearl: Safe in pregnancy: labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa, hydralazine. Avoid ACE inhibitors, ARBs and atenolol.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: The commonest site; forms endometriomas ('chocolate cysts').

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rarely involved; it is not among the typical sites of pelvic endometriosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A classic site in the pouch of Douglas, causing deep dyspareunia and nodularity on vaginal examination.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Extremely rare; distant sites more often reported are lung, umbilicus and scars.

questions.pearl: Commonest site of endometriosis is the ovary, followed by the pouch of Douglas and uterosacral ligaments.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Protein is markedly raised (often 1-5 g/L), sometimes forming a cobweb clot on standing.

options.label: B
options.explanation: CSF glucose falls to below about half of the blood glucose.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cells are mainly lymphocytes (mixed early); a neutrophil-predominant picture suggests bacterial meningitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Opening pressure is usually raised, often with hydrocephalus from basal exudates.

questions.pearl: TB meningitis CSF: lymphocytes, very high protein, low glucose, cobweb clot; ADA and GeneXpert help diagnosis.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Beta-hCG is markedly raised, often far above the level expected for gestation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hydropic villi give the classic snowstorm or bunch-of-grapes pattern of a complete mole.

options.label: C
options.text: Uterus larger than expected for dates
options.explanation: Seen in about half of complete moles due to vesicles and retained blood.

options.label: D
options.text: It is an abnormal form of pregnancy
options.explanation: It is gestational trophoblastic disease arising from abnormal fertilisation.

questions.pearl: Complete mole is 46XX, all paternal, no fetal parts; partial mole is triploid (69XXY) with fetal parts.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: An empty uterus with beta-hCG above the discriminatory zone (about 1500-2000 IU/L) strongly suggests ectopic pregnancy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pain usually comes first, followed by scanty dark vaginal bleeding; in abortion bleeding tends to precede pain.

options.label: C
options.text: Shoulder tip pain is an important feature
options.explanation: Haemoperitoneum irritates the diaphragm, giving referred pain via the phrenic nerve (C3-C5).

options.label: D
options.text: Incidence is more in women wearing an IUD
options.explanation: An IUD prevents intrauterine implantation better than tubal, so a pregnancy that occurs with an IUD is more likely ectopic.

questions.pearl: Classic triad of ectopic pregnancy: amenorrhoea, abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding; commonest site is the ampulla.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Small port incisions reduce pain, wound infection and dehiscence.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Magnified laparoscopic views usually improve visualisation; the limitation is loss of tactile feedback.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Haemostasis is more difficult laparoscopically and is a recognised limitation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The abdomen is not widely opened, so evaporative heat and fluid loss are reduced.

questions.pearl: Limitations of minimal access surgery: remote vision, poor haptics, difficult haemostasis, longer operating time, specimen extraction.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Normal vaginal pH is acidic, about 3.8-4.5, from lactic acid.

options.label: B
options.explanation: H2O2-producing lactobacilli inhibit anaerobes and protect against bacterial vaginosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Doderlein's bacilli (lactobacilli) are the dominant organisms in the reproductive years.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lactobacilli convert glycogen from oestrogenised epithelium into lactic acid.

questions.pearl: Loss of lactobacilli with pH above 4.5 favours bacterial vaginosis (Gardnerella), with clue cells and fishy odour.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ileal perforation of necrotic Peyer's patches occurs typically in the third week.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Salmonella typhi localises in the gallbladder, causing cholecystitis and the chronic carrier state.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Haematogenous spread can cause septic arthritis and osteomyelitis, particularly in sickle cell disease.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Toxic myocarditis is a recognised cardiovascular complication of enteric fever.

questions.pearl: Typhoid intestinal haemorrhage and perforation peak in the third week; the gallbladder is the carrier reservoir.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Avulsion is not a recognised complication of ovarian tumours.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The commonest complication, especially with mobile, medium-sized benign tumours such as dermoid cysts.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tumours may undergo haemorrhage, necrosis or degenerative change.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Benign tumours may undergo malignant transformation, e.g. squamous carcinoma in a dermoid.

questions.pearl: Complications of ovarian tumours: torsion, haemorrhage, rupture, infection, malignant change; dermoid is the commonest to tort.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets reflect severe endothelial injury.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Placental abruption (accidental haemorrhage) is a recognised complication of eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Glomerular endotheliosis, hypovolaemia and DIC can cause acute kidney injury.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A leading cause of maternal death in eclampsia, related to uncontrolled systolic pressure.

questions.pearl: Eclampsia maternal deaths: cerebral haemorrhage, pulmonary oedema, HELLP, abruption, renal failure; MgSO4 is the anticonvulsant of choice.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Large stroke volume with diastolic run-off gives the classic water-hammer pulse.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Aorta-to-pulmonary run-off in diastole widens pulse pressure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: VSD does not cause diastolic run-off from the aorta, so the pulse is not collapsing.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A hyperdynamic circulation with low peripheral resistance gives a bounding, collapsing pulse.

questions.pearl: Collapsing pulse: AR, PDA, AV fistula, and hyperdynamic states (anaemia, thyrotoxicosis, pregnancy, fever, Paget's).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sharing contaminated needles among injecting drug users is an efficient route.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lack of circumcision increases susceptibility, but it is not itself a route of transmission.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sexual transmission is the commonest route worldwide.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Transfusion of infected blood carries the highest per-exposure risk, over 90%.

questions.pearl: HIV is not transmitted by touching, kissing, food, insect bites, pools, coughing or sneezing.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Loop diuretics are not a recognised cause; spironolactone is the classic diuretic culprit.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reduced hepatic oestrogen clearance and increased peripheral aromatisation raise the oestrogen:androgen ratio.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Digoxin has an oestrogen-like structure and can cause gynaecomastia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Antiandrogenic effect by blocking androgen receptors.

questions.pearl: Drugs causing gynaecomastia, 'DISCO': digoxin, isoniazid, spironolactone, cimetidine, oestrogens.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Risks CO2 retention in type 2 respiratory failure; controlled oxygen targeting SpO2 88-92% is used.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Short- and long-acting beta-2 agonists are core bronchodilators.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Anticholinergic (antimuscarinic) bronchodilators such as tiotropium are used, not cholinergic drugs.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Improves exercise tolerance, breathlessness and quality of life.

questions.pearl: Only smoking cessation and long-term oxygen therapy (when indicated) improve survival in COPD.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Increases colonic ammonia production and absorption.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cause hypokalaemia, alkalosis and hypovolaemia, which increase renal ammonia generation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Benzodiazepines and opioids readily precipitate encephalopathy in cirrhosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hypokalaemia, not hyperkalaemia, precipitates encephalopathy by increasing renal ammoniagenesis.

questions.pearl: Precipitants of hepatic encephalopathy: GI bleed, infection, constipation, hypokalaemia, sedatives, dehydration, high protein load.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Thrombocytopenia (100,000 or less) is a defining criterion and counts can fall below 20,000 in severe disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A 20% or greater rise in haematocrit is evidence of plasma leakage, the hallmark of DHF.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A positive tourniquet test is a haemorrhagic manifestation in WHO criteria.

options.label: D
options.text: Platelet transfusion is a treatment option
options.explanation: Indicated with significant bleeding or very low counts (e.g. below 10,000); not given prophylactically otherwise.

questions.pearl: DHF = fever + haemorrhagic tendency + platelets 100,000 or less + plasma leakage (haematocrit rise 20%, effusions).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Test-and-treat is recommended for uninvestigated dyspepsia in younger patients without alarm features.

options.label: B
options.text: PPI use for more than 1 year
options.explanation: Long-term PPI users should be tested and treated, as H. pylori with acid suppression accelerates corpus atrophic gastritis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: First-degree relatives of gastric cancer patients should be eradicated to reduce cancer risk.

options.label: D
options.text: H. pylori positive with iron deficiency anaemia
options.explanation: Unexplained IDA is an accepted indication (Maastricht consensus).

questions.pearl: Firm indications: peptic ulcer, MALT lymphoma, gastric cancer prevention, unexplained IDA, ITP, long-term NSAID/PPI use.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Respiratory centres lie in the medulla and pons, not the hypothalamus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lung inflation inhibits inspiratory drive via the Hering-Breuer reflex rather than stimulating it.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Expiratory neurons of the ventral respiratory group fire during active (forced) expiration.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pneumotaxic and apneustic centres in the pons fine-tune the rhythm.

questions.pearl: Medullary dorsal group drives inspiration; the pneumotaxic centre (pons) limits inspiration and raises rate.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pain travels in the lateral spinothalamic tract.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Temperature also travels in the lateral spinothalamic tract.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Conscious proprioception is carried by the fasciculus gracilis and cuneatus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fine (discriminative) touch and vibration travel in the dorsal column-medial lemniscus pathway.

questions.pearl: Dorsal column lesion: loss of vibration and joint position sense, positive Romberg sign, sensory ataxia.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Adequate, predictable strength until the wound has healed is essential.

options.label: B
options.explanation: An ideal suture is non-allergenic with minimal tissue reaction.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Secure knots that do not slip are a key property.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Absorption should be predictable and matched to healing; rapid absorption risks dehiscence.

questions.pearl: Ideal suture: sterile, strong, easy to handle, secure knots, minimal reaction, non-capillary, non-allergenic, non-carcinogenic, cheap.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the usual urban cycle dengue passes man-mosquito-man without an animal reservoir; it is an anthroponosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Human malaria is man-mosquito-man; humans are the reservoir (P. knowlesi is the rare zoonotic exception).

options.label: C
options.explanation: In South Asia transmission is man-Aedes-man; it is classed as an arboviral anthroponosis in this setting.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A classic zoonosis transmitted to man from dogs and other animals.

questions.pearl: Zoonosis: disease naturally transmitted between vertebrate animals and man, e.g. rabies, anthrax, brucellosis, leptospirosis, plague.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: A dimorphic fungus causing systemic histoplasmosis, not a dermatophyte.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A lipophilic yeast causing pityriasis versicolor; not a dermatophyte.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Infects skin and nails but not hair.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Infects skin, hair and nails; the commonest dermatophyte genus.

questions.pearl: Dermatophyte genera: Trichophyton (skin, hair, nail), Microsporum (skin, hair), Epidermophyton (skin, nail).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Erythema with scaling and papulovesicles occurs, with scaling becoming more prominent as it settles.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Excoriations are typical of persistent itching in subacute and chronic eczema rather than the acute picture.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vesiculation with weeping, oozing and crusting characterises acute eczema.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Thickened skin with exaggerated markings results from chronic rubbing, a feature of chronic eczema.

questions.pearl: Acute eczema weeps (vesicles, exudate); chronic eczema thickens (lichenification, fissuring).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Intense generalised itch, worse at night, sparing the head in adults.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Itch is common in psoriasis and can be widespread.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Characteristically very itchy, often widespread purple polygonal papules.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Head lice cause localised scalp itch rather than generalised pruritus.

questions.pearl: Systemic causes of generalised pruritus without rash: cholestasis, CKD, iron deficiency, polycythaemia, lymphoma, thyroid disease.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The dermis derives from mesoderm (dermatome); the epidermis is ectodermal.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Derived from paraxial mesoderm (myotomes of somites).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hepatocytes come from endoderm of the foregut, although its stroma is mesodermal.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Respiratory epithelium arises from foregut endoderm.

questions.pearl: Endoderm forms gut and respiratory epithelium, liver and pancreas; mesoderm forms muscle, bone, blood, kidney and gonads.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Somatic cells divide by mitosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Somatic tissue; mature fibres are post-mitotic.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Spermatogonia multiply by mitosis; meiosis begins in the primary spermatocyte.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Primary oocytes enter meiosis I in fetal life and arrest in prophase I until ovulation.

questions.pearl: Meiosis I is completed at ovulation (secondary oocyte), meiosis II only after fertilisation.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Routine OCP use is not emergency contraception; the old Yuzpe regimen is now largely replaced.

options.label: B
options.explanation: 1.5 mg single dose within 72 hours (licensed up to 120 h, less effective).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Used for medical treatment of ectopic pregnancy, not emergency contraception.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Selective progesterone receptor modulator, 30 mg within 120 hours; more effective than levonorgestrel.

questions.pearl: Most effective emergency contraceptive: copper IUD within 5 days of intercourse.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Malignant infiltration of the hilum causes relentless obstructive jaundice.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Progressive painless jaundice with a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier's law).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hilar or distal bile duct tumours cause steadily deepening jaundice.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Stones cause intermittent jaundice, as the stone can float back and relieve the obstruction.

questions.pearl: Jaundice patterns: intermittent (CBD stone), fluctuating (periampullary carcinoma), progressive (Ca pancreas head, cholangiocarcinoma).

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Causes of acute diarrhoea in children:

options.label: A
options.explanation: ETEC and other diarrhoeagenic E. coli are major bacterial causes in developing countries.

options.label: B
options.explanation: S. aureus causes toxin-mediated food poisoning with vomiting predominant; not a usual cause of childhood diarrhoea.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The commonest cause of severe dehydrating diarrhoea in under-fives.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A common cause of bloody diarrhoea in children; linked to Guillain-Barre syndrome.

questions.pearl: Rotavirus is the commonest cause of acute watery diarrhoea in infants; Shigella is the commonest cause of dysentery.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: The first 7 days is the early neonatal period, not the whole neonatal period.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The neonatal period covers the first 28 days of life.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not a defined period.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The late neonatal period is 7-28 days.

questions.pearl: Perinatal period: 28 weeks gestation to 7 days after birth; neonatal: first 28 days; infancy: first year.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: An NSAID that reduces menstrual blood loss by about 25-30% and relieves dysmenorrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Antifibrinolytic reducing blood loss by about 50%.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cyclical progestogens or the LNG-IUS are used; the LNG-IUS is first-line in many guidelines.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Combined OCP reduces menstrual loss and regulates cycles.

questions.pearl: LNG-IUS (Mirena) is the most effective medical treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hyaline cartilage contains type II collagen; type I is in fibrocartilage, bone and skin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cartilage is avascular and nourished by diffusion from the perichondrium or synovial fluid.

options.label: C
options.text: Forms the epiphyseal plate of growing bones
options.explanation: The growth plate is hyaline cartilage undergoing endochondral ossification.

options.label: D
options.text: Covers the articular surface of bone
options.explanation: Articular cartilage of synovial joints is hyaline (without perichondrium).

questions.pearl: Type I collagen: bone, skin, tendon; type II: hyaline cartilage, vitreous; type III: reticular; type IV: basement membrane.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Risk factors for carcinoma of the cervix:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dietary fat is linked to breast and endometrial cancer, not cervical cancer.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Increases exposure to high-risk HPV types 16 and 18.

options.label: C
options.explanation: High parity is an established cofactor for cervical cancer.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Carcinogens concentrate in cervical mucus and impair local immunity.

questions.pearl: HPV 16 and 18 cause about 70% of cervical cancers; early coitus, multiple partners, smoking and immunosuppression add risk.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The first ACE inhibitor; contains a sulfhydryl group (rash, taste disturbance).

options.label: B
options.explanation: A prodrug converted to enalaprilat.

options.label: C
options.explanation: An angiotensin II receptor (AT1) blocker; it does not cause bradykinin-mediated cough.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A long-acting ACE inhibitor shown to reduce cardiovascular events (HOPE trial).

questions.pearl: ACE inhibitors end in -pril, ARBs in -sartan; ACEI cough and angioedema are due to bradykinin accumulation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Causes of abnormal bleeding during pregnancy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Causes painless, recurrent bright red antepartum haemorrhage.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Presents with acute pain and vomiting, not vaginal bleeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Painful bleeding with blood escaping through the cervix.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Coagulopathies such as von Willebrand disease or ITP can cause bleeding in pregnancy.

questions.pearl: APH = bleeding from the genital tract after 28 weeks (24 weeks in some guidelines) and before delivery of the baby.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Causes of first trimester vaginal bleeding:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Oestrogen-driven ectropion is friable and bleeds, especially after intercourse.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A local cause of bleeding that must be excluded on speculum examination.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The commonest cause of first trimester bleeding.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Placenta praevia causes bleeding in the third trimester (after 28 weeks), not the first.

questions.pearl: First trimester bleeding: abortion, ectopic, molar pregnancy, implantation bleed, local cervical lesions.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with upper abdominal pain and several episodes of vomiting. Possible causes:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back with repeated vomiting; check serum lipase or amylase.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Causes lower abdominal pain with vaginal discharge and fever.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Causes dysuria, frequency and suprapubic or loin pain.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Epigastric pain with vomiting, especially with gastric outlet obstruction or complications.

questions.pearl: Raised serum lipase three times or more the upper limit is more specific than amylase for acute pancreatitis.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Vomiting is usually limited to one or two episodes after pain begins; profuse vomiting suggests obstruction or gastroenteritis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pain classically starts periumbilical and migrates to the right iliac fossa as the parietal peritoneum becomes involved.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tenderness at McBurney's point with guarding and rebound is the key sign.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Low-grade fever is common; high fever suggests perforation.

questions.pearl: Murphy's triad of appendicitis: pain, then vomiting, then fever. Alvarado score aids diagnosis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: A phagocyte of innate immunity.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mediates humoral immunity and differentiates into antibody-secreting plasma cells.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mediates cell-mediated immunity with antigen-specific receptors and memory.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Natural killer cells are innate lymphocytes lacking antigen-specific receptors.

questions.pearl: Adaptive immunity is specific and has memory; innate cells include neutrophils, macrophages, dendritic, mast and NK cells.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Not a feature; cardiovascular involvement is aortic root dilatation, dissection and mitral valve prolapse.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Upward and outward lens dislocation from weak zonules (fibrillin-1 defect).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Intelligence is normal; lens dislocation with intellectual disability suggests homocystinuria.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Long spider-like fingers, with positive thumb and wrist signs.

questions.pearl: Marfan: FBN1 mutation, autosomal dominant; lens dislocates upwards (homocystinuria: downwards).

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fatty liver with hepatomegaly is a feature of kwashiorkor, not marasmus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Loss of buccal fat gives the monkey-like or old man facies.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of gluteal fat and muscle leaves loose skin folds over the buttocks.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Flaky-paint dermatosis is characteristic of kwashiorkor.

questions.pearl: Marasmus: severe wasting without oedema, alert and hungry; kwashiorkor: oedema, dermatosis, hair changes, fatty liver, apathy.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Conjunctivitis causes superficial conjunctival congestion; ciliary congestion suggests keratitis, iritis or glaucoma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Adenoviral conjunctivitis typically has watery discharge with follicles and preauricular nodes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Marked chemosis is typical of allergic or severe bacterial conjunctivitis rather than viral.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Itching is the hallmark of allergic conjunctivitis and is usually absent in viral disease.

questions.pearl: Discharge type: watery (viral), mucopurulent (bacterial), ropy mucoid (allergic). Follicles favour viral or chlamydial.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Typically unilateral and pulsating, though it can switch sides.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Photophobia and phonophobia are part of the diagnostic criteria.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not a feature; transient weakness occurs only in the rare hemiplegic migraine.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Classically unilateral in adults, although bilateral pain is common in children.

questions.pearl: Migraine without aura: at least 5 attacks of 4-72 h headache with 2 of unilateral, pulsating, moderate-severe, worse with activity.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Photosensitive dermatitis, e.g. Casal's necklace.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Neuropsychiatric changes ranging from insomnia to dementia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Glossitis and diarrhoea from mucosal involvement.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Untreated pellagra progresses to death, the fourth 'D'.

questions.pearl: Pellagra (niacin, B3 deficiency): the 4 Ds; also seen in Hartnup disease, carcinoid syndrome and isoniazid therapy.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Symptoms and signs of brain tumour:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raised intracranial pressure is worst after lying flat overnight.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Part of Cushing's response (hypertension, bradycardia, irregular breathing) to raised ICP.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Optic disc swelling from raised intracranial pressure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Can occur with bilateral corticospinal tract involvement or brainstem compression.

questions.pearl: Raised ICP triad: headache worse in the morning, vomiting, papilloedema.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Vasodilatation and capillary leak cause hypotension, not hypertension.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Laryngeal oedema and spasm cause stridor and airway obstruction.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not a feature of an IgE-mediated anaphylactic reaction.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Distributive shock is a defining feature.

questions.pearl: Anaphylaxis: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg (1:1000) into the anterolateral thigh, repeat after 5 minutes if needed.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: A 2-year-old child presents with severe chest indrawing. Most likely classification:

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the IMCI chart this item refers to, chest indrawing upgrades the classification beyond simple pneumonia (revised WHO 2014 guidance differs).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chest indrawing is classified as severe pneumonia or very severe disease in the IMCI chart.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cough or cold has no fast breathing and no chest indrawing.

options.label: D
options.explanation: With any general danger sign, chest indrawing falls into severe pneumonia or very severe disease; refer urgently.

questions.pearl: Fast breathing cut-offs: 60/min under 2 months, 50/min 2-12 months, 40/min 1-5 years.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: After massive transfusion, citrate metabolism causes alkalosis and potassium shifts into cells, so hypokalaemia can follow.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acute haemolytic reactions release free haemoglobin and cause acute kidney injury.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hepatitis B and C, HIV, syphilis, malaria and bacterial contamination can be transmitted.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Potassium leaks from stored red cells, a risk with rapid or massive transfusion.

questions.pearl: Massive transfusion: coagulopathy, hypothermia, hypocalcaemia (citrate), hyper/hypokalaemia, acidosis, ARDS.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Commonest intraocular malignancy of childhood (RB1 gene); presents with leukocoria.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A small round cell bone tumour of children and adolescents, t(11;22).

options.label: C
options.explanation: The childhood primary liver malignancy is hepatoblastoma; HCC is mainly an adult tumour.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A tumour of older, sun-exposed adults.

questions.pearl: Commonest childhood malignancy: acute lymphoblastic leukaemia; commonest solid tumour: brain tumours, then neuroblastoma.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Short, shuffling steps that hurry forward with a stooped posture.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Small, cramped handwriting reflects bradykinesia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The face is expressionless and mask-like (hypomimia) with reduced blinking.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lead-pipe rigidity with superimposed tremor gives the cogwheel quality.

questions.pearl: Parkinsonism requires bradykinesia plus rest tremor or rigidity; the rest tremor is 4-6 Hz pill-rolling.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: A fine tremor is a common somatic symptom of sympathetic overactivity.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A recognised psychological symptom of severe anxiety.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Autonomic arousal causes sweating, palpitations and dizziness.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Initial insomnia (difficulty falling asleep) is typical; early morning waking suggests depression.

questions.pearl: Anxiety causes initial insomnia; depression causes early morning awakening.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rachitic rosary belongs to rickets; scurvy gives a sharper, angulated scorbutic rosary.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Not a characteristic feature; gum changes and loosening of teeth occur instead.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Defective collagen synthesis causes swollen, spongy gums that bleed easily.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Not a prominent feature; subperiosteal haemorrhage, bone pain and pseudoparalysis predominate.

questions.pearl: Scurvy (vitamin C deficiency): perifollicular haemorrhage, corkscrew hairs, bleeding gums, poor wound healing.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: It enters the deep ring and traverses the inguinal canal within the spermatic cord.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Indirect hernias commonly descend into the scrotum (complete or scrotal hernia).

options.label: C
options.text: Lies medial to the inferior epigastric vessels
options.explanation: The indirect sac lies lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels; direct hernias lie medial.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Commonest in children and young adults, from a patent processus vaginalis; direct hernias occur in older men.

questions.pearl: Deep ring occlusion test: if the hernia is controlled by pressure over the deep ring, it is indirect.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: The earliest and most important symptom in a woman with regular cycles.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nausea and vomiting typically from about 6 weeks, linked to rising hCG.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Heartburn is mainly a feature of later pregnancy as the uterus enlarges.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The enlarging anteverted uterus presses on the bladder in the first trimester.

questions.pearl: Frequency of micturition appears in the first trimester, disappears in the second, and returns near term.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Masseter spasm (lockjaw) is often the first sign.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Generalised spasm of back extensors arches the body.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The neurotoxin is tetanospasmin, which blocks inhibitory GABA and glycine release; tetanolysin is a haemolysin.

options.label: D
options.text: Prophylaxis by vaccine (tetanus toxoid) and TIG
options.explanation: Tetanus-prone wounds receive toxoid and human tetanus immunoglobulin according to immunisation status.

questions.pearl: Tetanospasmin travels retrogradely to the spinal cord and blocks inhibitory interneurons, causing rigidity and spasms.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: The oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve shifts to the right with:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Heat lowers haemoglobin's oxygen affinity, unloading oxygen in active tissues.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Bohr effect: CO2 and H+ reduce oxygen affinity.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Acidosis shifts the curve right.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Exercise raises temperature, CO2, H+ and 2,3-DPG, all of which shift the curve right.

questions.pearl: Right shift 'CADET face right': CO2, acid, 2,3-DPG, exercise, temperature. Fetal Hb and stored blood shift left.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Not a standard step in water purification.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Storage or the three-pot method lets suspended particles settle.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chlorination, boiling or solar disinfection kills pathogens.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Slow and rapid sand filters remove particles and many organisms.

questions.pearl: Large-scale purification: storage, filtration (slow or rapid sand), then disinfection (chlorination).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Moist heat at 100 C kills vegetative bacteria but not all spores; listed among physical methods.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Moist heat below 100 C (63 C for 30 min or 72 C for 15 s), a physical method.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A chemical disinfectant, not a physical method.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ionising (gamma) and non-ionising (UV) radiation are physical methods.

questions.pearl: Autoclave: 121 C at 15 psi for 15 minutes; spores of Geobacillus stearothermophilus are used as the indicator.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble at the apex with presystolic accentuation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Early diastolic decrescendo murmur at the left sternal edge.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Gives an ejection systolic murmur that increases with Valsalva.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A functional mid-diastolic mitral murmur caused by the AR jet in severe aortic regurgitation.

questions.pearl: Diastolic murmurs are always pathological; Graham Steell is the early diastolic murmur of pulmonary regurgitation.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Respiratory viruses cause the majority of acute bronchitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Influenza and parainfluenza are common viral causes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not a usual cause of acute bronchitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: One of the atypical bacterial causes, with Mycoplasma and Bordetella.

questions.pearl: Acute bronchitis is mostly viral; antibiotics are not routinely needed.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Simple febrile seizures are generalised, usually tonic-clonic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Simple seizures last under 15 minutes; longer duration makes them complex.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Recurrence within 24 hours defines a complex febrile seizure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The child is neurologically and developmentally normal.

questions.pearl: Febrile seizures occur at 6 months to 5 years; complex = focal, over 15 minutes, or recurrent within 24 hours.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: High-risk types 16 and 18 cause cervical, anal and oropharyngeal carcinoma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Not directly oncogenic; it raises cancer risk indirectly through immunosuppression (via HHV-8, EBV, HPV).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Linked to nasopharyngeal carcinoma, Burkitt and Hodgkin lymphoma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chronic HCV infection leads to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

questions.pearl: Oncogenic infections: HPV, EBV, HBV, HCV, HHV-8, HTLV-1, H. pylori, Schistosoma haematobium, Clonorchis.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Left supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is seen in:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Virchow's node (Troisier's sign) from spread via the thoracic duct.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Myeloma is a marrow disease; lymphadenopathy is not a feature.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Giant cell tumour is locally aggressive and rarely spreads to lymph nodes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Testicular tumours drain to para-aortic nodes and may spread via the thoracic duct to the left supraclavicular node.

questions.pearl: Virchow's node collects lymph from the abdomen and pelvis via the thoracic duct: stomach, pancreas, testis, ovary.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Not a usual cause of haemoptysis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hypertrophied bronchial arteries can cause recurrent and massive haemoptysis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Asthma does not cause haemoptysis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The commonest cause of haemoptysis in Bangladesh; also Rasmussen's aneurysm in cavities.

questions.pearl: Massive haemoptysis arises mostly from bronchial arteries; bronchial artery embolisation is the first-line intervention.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The 'guardian of the genome', mutated in about half of human cancers (Li-Fraumeni syndrome).

options.label: B
options.explanation: A proto-oncogene; gain-of-function mutations occur in pancreatic and colorectal cancers.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss causes familial adenomatous polyposis and starts the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A proto-oncogene; gain-of-function mutations cause MEN 2 and medullary thyroid carcinoma.

questions.pearl: Tumour suppressors: RB, TP53, APC, BRCA1/2, WT1, NF1, VHL. Oncogenes: RAS, MYC, RET, HER2, BCR-ABL.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Attacks of rotatory vertigo lasting minutes to hours.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fluctuating low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A sense of pressure in the ear accompanies attacks.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Low-pitched roaring tinnitus is part of the classic tetrad.

questions.pearl: Meniere's disease is endolymphatic hydrops: vertigo, fluctuating SNHL, tinnitus and aural fullness.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Optic nerve compression or involvement can impair vision; an emergency sign.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Axial proptosis differentiates orbital from preseptal cellulitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A relative afferent pupillary defect may develop with optic nerve dysfunction.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Restricted, painful eye movements are characteristic of orbital involvement.

questions.pearl: Orbital cellulitis commonly spreads from the ethmoid sinus; complications include cavernous sinus thrombosis.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: An age-related loss of accommodation, classified as an anomaly of accommodation, not a refractive error.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Parallel rays focus behind the retina; corrected with convex lenses.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Unequal refraction in different meridians; corrected with cylindrical lenses.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A developmental corneal enlargement, not a refractive error.

questions.pearl: Refractive errors: myopia (concave lens), hypermetropia (convex lens), astigmatism (cylindrical lens).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Stapes footplate fixation causes progressive conductive deafness with Carhart's notch.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Causes unilateral sensorineural (retrocochlear) hearing loss.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Meniere's disease causes sensorineural hearing loss.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Effusion or tympanic membrane perforation impairs sound conduction.

questions.pearl: Rinne negative and Weber lateralised to the affected ear indicate conductive deafness.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Therapeutic products of recombinant DNA technology:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Recombinant interferons, interleukins and monoclonal antibodies are used in cancer therapy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Recombinant viral and plasmid vectors deliver therapeutic genes in gene therapy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Recombinant monoclonal antibodies such as rituximab and trastuzumab are widely used.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Recombinant human GH (somatropin) replaced cadaveric pituitary GH.

questions.pearl: First recombinant drug approved: human insulin (1982), produced in E. coli.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Substances actively reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Almost completely reabsorbed by sodium-coupled secondary active transport.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reabsorbed by SGLT2 and SGLT1 up to the transport maximum (renal threshold about 180 mg/dL).

options.label: C
options.explanation: About 65% of filtered sodium is actively reabsorbed in the PCT via the basolateral Na-K ATPase.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Freely filtered and slightly secreted, not reabsorbed; hence its use to estimate GFR.

questions.pearl: PCT reabsorbs 100% of glucose and amino acids, about 65% of Na and water, and most HCO3.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Close K-ATP channels on beta cells, depolarising them and releasing insulin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: PPAR-gamma agonists that improve insulin sensitivity; they do not release insulin.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Metformin reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis and does not cause hypoglycaemia alone.

options.label: D
options.explanation: An alpha-glucosidase inhibitor that slows carbohydrate absorption in the gut.

questions.pearl: Secretagogues: sulfonylureas and meglitinides (repaglinide, nateglinide); GLP-1 agonists and DPP-4 inhibitors raise insulin glucose-dependently.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Bioavailability of an orally administered drug:

options.label: A
options.explanation: A drug must dissolve to be absorbed; poorly soluble drugs have low bioavailability.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Smaller particles have greater surface area and dissolve faster (e.g. micronised griseofulvin).

options.label: C
options.text: Is not influenced by the presence of food
options.explanation: Food can reduce (e.g. ampicillin) or increase (e.g. griseofulvin with fatty food) absorption.

options.label: D
options.text: Does not depend on disintegration time
options.explanation: A tablet must disintegrate before it dissolves; formulation affects bioavailability.

questions.pearl: Oral bioavailability is reduced by first-pass hepatic metabolism, e.g. nitroglycerin, propranolol, lidocaine.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Gastric acid secretion is increased by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Stimulates parietal cells directly and via histamine release from ECL cells.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Vagal ACh acts on M3 receptors of parietal cells.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The cephalic phase, mediated by the vagus, accounts for about 30% of acid secretion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Glucagon inhibits rather than stimulates gastric acid secretion.

questions.pearl: Acid stimulants: ACh, gastrin, histamine. Inhibitors: somatostatin, secretin, GIP, prostaglandins.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Magnesium sulphate can be used as:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Drug of choice to prevent and treat eclamptic fits (Pritchard or Zuspan regimen).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Given before 32 weeks of preterm birth to reduce the risk of cerebral palsy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Relaxes uterine muscle by competing with calcium, although its tocolytic efficacy is limited.

options.label: D
options.explanation: It has no antiemetic role.

questions.pearl: MgSO4 toxicity: loss of patellar reflex first, then respiratory depression; antidote is 10% calcium gluconate 10 mL IV.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Tissue-invasive helminths are the commonest cause of eosinophilia worldwide.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Not a typical cause of eosinophilia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Causes atypical lymphocytosis, not eosinophilia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: IL-5 production by Reed-Sternberg cells causes eosinophilia.

questions.pearl: Eosinophilia causes: allergy, helminths, drugs, vasculitis (EGPA), Hodgkin lymphoma, hypereosinophilic syndrome, Addison's.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cellular swelling from Na-K pump failure is the earliest reversible change.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Injured cells show increased eosinophilia from loss of RNA and denatured proteins.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Membrane breakdown is a feature of irreversible injury (necrosis).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Accumulation of lipid vacuoles, e.g. in hepatocytes, is reversible.

questions.pearl: Irreversible injury hallmarks: severe mitochondrial damage, membrane rupture, nuclear pyknosis, karyorrhexis, karyolysis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Venous thrombi in slow-flowing veins usually fill and occlude the lumen.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Venous (red) thrombi are rich in red cells within fibrin; arterial thrombi are platelet-rich.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pelvic venous plexuses such as the periprostatic plexus are recognised sites.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lines of Zahn form in thrombi in flowing blood; they are present, though less distinct, in venous thrombi.

questions.pearl: Lines of Zahn distinguish an antemortem thrombus from a postmortem clot.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Constipation in diabetes relates to autonomic neuropathy rather than nephropathy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Increased gut motility causes frequent stools or diarrhoea.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypercalcaemia, not hypocalcaemia, causes constipation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Spinal cord and autonomic involvement commonly causes constipation.

questions.pearl: Metabolic causes of constipation: hypothyroidism, hypercalcaemia, hypokalaemia, diabetes, pregnancy.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Painless urinary retention with overflow is a key red flag.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Loss of perineal sensation (S2-S5) is classic.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A lower motor neurone lesion causes reduced or absent ankle reflexes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Root compression causes bilateral lower limb weakness and sensory loss.

questions.pearl: Cauda equina syndrome is a surgical emergency: urgent MRI and decompression within 48 hours.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Complications that may arise after total gastrectomy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Loss of reservoir capacity causes early satiety and weight loss.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Protein digestion continues via pancreatic proteases in the small bowel.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Not a typical complication; dumping and diarrhoea are more common.

options.label: D
options.text: Depletion of vitamin B12 stored in the liver
options.explanation: Loss of intrinsic factor means hepatic B12 stores run down over several years.

questions.pearl: After total gastrectomy give lifelong IM vitamin B12; also watch for iron deficiency, dumping and osteoporosis.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: HBV is parenterally transmitted; faeco-oral spread is a feature of hepatitis A and E.

options.label: B
options.explanation: There is no animal reservoir or transmission via dogs.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HBV is present in semen and vaginal secretions.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Vertical transmission from HBsAg-positive (especially HBeAg-positive) mothers is a major route.

questions.pearl: Newborns of HBsAg-positive mothers need HBV vaccine plus HBIG within 12 hours of birth.
